newsitem.title: Bangladesh: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - June 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - June 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) chief and former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia on Monday said the government was implementing plans "of its foreign masters".
Port users have threatened to launch a fresh boycott programme at the Chittagong Port from next week to press their demand for the use of private equipment at the port.
Opposition BNP, which had boycotted earlier parliamentary by-elections, on Monday decided to contest the June 30 by-polls in a Manikganj constituency.
Bangladesh and South Korea on Monday signed an agreement under which Seoul will provide a loan of $33 million for purchasing of 19 meter gauge electric locomotives for Bangladesh Railways.
Civil bureaucrats have welcomed the decison of two-day weekend in Bangladesh.
Bangladesh's central bank on Sunday issued licenses to 16 money changers.
Soap manufacturers are seeking reduction of duty on palm stearin, a basic raw material for soap, to make the product more competitive and hygienic.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has asked manufacturers and exporters of readymade garments to be more competitive. REUTER
